findings.summary: AI seat says 'Pending · Choosing a deck' with a green 'Choose its deck' button: the host must choose for the AI

localEvidence.detail: P exercises host-authorized deterministic auto-assignment through real existing known/deck command shapes, validates a public precon before assignment, skips assigned seats and preserves manual override. No private deck list or model call. With no eligible deck/server failure, the UI reports a recoverable failure rather than falsely claiming selection. No later seat-kind endpoint exists.

findings.summary: The chooser lists 'Shared decks' and 'Your library decks' with the same decks appearing in both under different names (D3 Kiora vs D3 Kasmina, D5 Teysa Karlov vs D5 Shadrix)

localEvidence.detail: Follow-up `f81ae7ca`; P + T155 prove one Your decks list using current library names, exact expanded commander/card-multiset matching removes stale-name shared duplicates, differing quantities/contents remain Shared with the table, and distinct local deck IDs are never merged by name. The shared projection exposes no source ID, so contents are compared rather than inventing identity. The labeled Only table-legal decks filter defaults on and remembers explicit opt-out; final server admission remains authoritative. Six public precons remain separately available in their catalog disclosure. `work/r4-shots/chooser-canonical-shared-1400.png` inspected; its same-name shared row is deliberately a different-content fixture, not the stale duplicate. Existing permission recheck and no-import submission path retained.

localEvidence.detail: D verifies Outcome/Card that won it first, deck bracket and last-game pod/seat prefill; no false fixed B2 assumption. This is a bounded form-behavior proof, not a six-theme audit of all eleven controls and required semantics.

localEvidence.detail: A displays bounded invite rows and distinct admission/delivery states using the existing invitation mutation contract. No invented resend/revoke or feature-switch writes. It does not send real mail, prove provider delivery, or cover every post-Send wording state.

findings.summary: The Budget card lists 30+ deck rows with Budget / Cost / Counts and dominates the right column above AI Coach, Data and the Danger zone

localEvidence.detail: C intentionally preserves the existing per-deck budget table and asserts that every live deck is listed. No collapse/filter or density redesign was implemented. Responsive stacking alone does not resolve the original 30-deck dominance complaint.

findings.summary: 'Clear all data' is a one-click button with a caption ('Save a backup first.'); 'Delete account' asks for the typed address

localEvidence.detail: C opens the danger-fill confirmation and requires typed CLEAR; existing Delete account typed-address semantics retained. No one-click destructive clear.

findings.summary: 'Reduce motion' and 'Stop at every step of my turn' are buttons whose on/off state is not visible

localEvidence.detail: C exercises persisted visible On/Off plus role=switch/aria-checked for both controls. Play owns the step-toggle markup; Workshop acceptance ran with that dependency integrated.

findings.summary: Settings is reached from three places with three labels: 'Settings' (menu), 'Profile' (pill), 'Account & app settings' (board avatar menu)

localEvidence.detail: S/C/AM verify the single shared Settings entry and identical native menu markup in both entry documents. The global menu has You / This device / Your data / Skin / Help / Careful / final Sign out, with verified Invite/Admin in You. The board must call the shared hooks and guard its own hotkeys; AM proves alternate/redrawn invoker behavior but does not substitute for the separately owned real board-avatar/target-draft acceptance. Explicit Play settings remains a distinct Camera control per EX-10.

findings.summary: The Confirmations dialog has no controls: 'Every step still asks before it acts.' plus a note

localEvidence.detail: C verifies four explanatory RQ-12 way-back rows. Packet and EX-08 explicitly require read-only capability classes until actually switchable; no fake preference controls were added. Existing restore-confirmation controls remain only where a supported saved skip exists.

findings.summary: The 'Actions' row is disabled with no reason, and the drag handles promised by the caption are not visible in the matrix

localEvidence.detail: The Side Drawer Modules implementation belongs to Play. Workshop's Settings run verifies its entry, not a complete matrix interaction/handle/disabled-reason audit. No resolution is inferred from CH-87 or the retained entry.

findings.summary: 'Saved view preferences' fills the history (11 of the first 13 rows) and 'Undo last change' would undo a view preference rather than a library change

localEvidence.detail: History filters preference noise; K proves preferences create no persistent Undo receipt and any intervening revision invalidates a prior receipt. The generic existing Settings Undo-last-change command still addresses repository transaction order; this work does not establish that it skips all preference transactions.

findings.summary: The seven tours are the best onboarding surface in the app and the only door to them is a menu row 17 rows deep

localEvidence.detail: Take a tour is exposed in page Help and quietly on Landing; L/J exercise the landing surface. Existing tour definitions and action path are reused; no assertion that every tour's entire content was replayed in this pass.

findings.summary: A targets question shows no source → effect → target relationship: the desk draws the acting card and lists the targets as text buttons
Focusing an opponent's board is a 14 px-tall link ('View AI's board, 40 life', 1345×14) in Full view and 59×24 '⤢ Focus' buttons at 11 px in Table view; no pointer gesture on the board itself
Side-pane modules have fixed heights; the only drag handle is the pane's width ('Actions and boards width: drag, or use the arrow keys', 12×797)
The Coach header on main is about four times the height it needs ('CrankMagic Coach · Sees your board, hand and the table · turn 1'); production's is one 49 px line
The four prompt chips are 11 px text in 26 px-tall targets; on main they are hidden altogether
Module reorder in edit mode relies on a six-dot drag handle that is small and does not work well; the ↑ ↓ buttons already do the job
Module headers are not toggles: collapsing a side-pane module is a separate 33×40 button at 12 px, and a collapsed module cannot be resized
Prepared: after the creature half resolves prepared, the option to cast the copy as its spell half is not offered (Studious First-Year)
The block draft is blocker-first with text pairs ('Goblin #486 → Dream Stalker #475 · Remove'), a 'Clear this blocker' button, 'All block options' and one Confirm for the whole draft
Target options name the card and append the controller as a suffix only for permanents that are not yours ('Smuggler's Copter (Keith's)'); nothing groups targets by player

During a targets question the desk's large image is the source card and the title repeats its name ('Reclamation Sage: choose one target …'); the affected card is only a text button, and a second Confirm / Clear step follows
Identical lands render as separate cards on the battlefield; #878 stacks identical options only inside a question
The lands / battlefield split within a board is fixed, while three other dimensions already drag (pane width, boards' widths, hand size)
